protocol.description:
This protocol allows a client to query and configure displays managed by the NVIDIA Display Config Server (DCS).
Warning: This protocol is unstable and subject to change without notice.

interface.name: zwp_dcs_manager
interface.description: This object is where the usage begins. The configuration tool will connect to the wayland socket and create a new manager object. This manager object is used to get the DCS companion object to a given wl_output advertised by the system. It is also used to create topology objects which are used for atomically updating the system state.

request.name: get_output

description.summary: create a zwp_dcs_output for a wl_output

request.description: Creates a zwp_dcs_output object which extends the provided wl_output.

request.name: create_topology
request.description: Creates a zwp_dcs_topology object which is used to atomically commit configuration changes across multiple displays.

interface.name: zwp_dcs_output
interface.description:
This object is used to describe the current physical display count and layout. It extends wl_output, meaning wayland global objects visible in wl_registry will be added and removed to reflect the current display state. Most of the display information comes from wl_output, however this allows us to attach display config server specific information to each output.
Note that the events here will be resent on any changes. Unlike wl_output's values which are sent once, these may be resent if there have been any changes.

entry.name: none
entry.summary: an available but non-active, non-preferred mode

entry.name: current
entry.summary: this is the currently set mode for this display

entry.name: preferred
entry.summary: this is the native (first-listed) mode and refresh rate

event.name: mode
event.description: Sends a supported mode for this output. The mode flags indicate whether this is the currently active mode or the preferred (native) mode.

event.name: device

description.summary: the DRM device for this output

event.description: The device that this output is connected to, expressed as a dev_t device number.

event.name: number
event.description: The ID number (1-n) of the display.

event.name: done

description.summary: all DCS output state has been sent

event.description: Signals that all DCS output state has finished sending.

request.name: create_configuration
request.description: Create a new zwp_dcs_display_configuration object for this output.

interface.name: zwp_dcs_display_configuration
interface.description:
This object allows for configuring one display in the system. It takes care of updating only one display and will be part of a broader topology update which will control setting multiple configurations across multiple displays/devices. Think of this like a description of display state which will be applied during an atomic topology commit.
The configuration only needs to include the pieces of state which need to be changed. Values which are omitted will not have their state changed from what the display is currently using.

entry.name: invalid_state
entry.summary: a component of this double-buffered commit could not be applied

request.name: set_mode
request.description: Records the requested mode to set with this configuration update.

event.name: error
event.description: Error returned on this object if part of its configuration failed.

interface.name: zwp_dcs_topology
interface.description: A topology combines multiple zwp_dcs_display_configuration objects into one atomic state commit. These configs represent changes to an individual display and the topology represents changes to the entire display wall. The topology has a set of configs added to it, then once everything is specified the topology is committed. If there are any issues with the attempted configuration change then the topology will return an error event signaling failure, and the specific display_configuration objects causing the problem will receive error events to hint what caused the commit to be rejected.

entry.name: failed
entry.summary: a component of this double-buffered commit could not be applied; the configuration objects will have an error posted to disclose more

entry.name: duplicate_configs
entry.summary: multiple configurations were added that reference the same output object

request.name: add_configuration

description.summary: add a configuration to the topology

request.description: Adds a configuration to the topology to be committed.

request.name: commit
request.description: Commits the changes to all configurations.

event.name: error
event.description: Error returned on this object if part of its configuration failed.
